covers: The registers of the 8253 and 8254 interval timer

entries.name: counter 0
entries.description: Counter 0 of the interval timer: a 16-bit down counter loaded by a write and read back by a read.
entries.behaviour: A write loads the count and a read returns it, one byte at a time in the order the control word chose: low byte, high byte, or low then high. In mode 3 a read returns an even value.

sources.ref: datasheet:Intel 8254 datasheet, https://www.scs.stanford.edu/10wi-cs140/pintos/specs/8254.pdf, Figure 7 Control Word Format

entries.name: counter 1
entries.description: Counter 1 of the interval timer: a 16-bit down counter loaded by a write and read back by a read.
entries.behaviour: A write loads the count and a read returns it, one byte at a time in the order the control word chose: low byte, high byte, or low then high. In mode 3 a read returns an even value.
entries.differs: On the IBM PC DOSBox-X installs no write handler for it (the line is commented out) and only a read handler; MAME handles both.

entries.name: control word
entries.description: The control word register: it sets a counter's mode, access order and counting base, and carries the latch and read-back commands. It can only be written.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7-6 select the counter (3 is the 8254 read-back command), bits 5-4 the access (0 latches the count), bits 3-1 the mode (6 and 7 act as 2 and 3) and bit 0 BCD counting. Writing it stops that counter until a count is loaded.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X latches the count of every counter a read-back selects but the status of only the first; MAME's 8254 latches both for each, and its 8253 ignores read-back.

sources.ref: datasheet:Intel 8254 datasheet, https://www.scs.stanford.edu/10wi-cs140/pintos/specs/8254.pdf, Figure 7 Control Word Format
